authorization: User explicitly requested further improvement iteration after the failed memory study. This is a new study; the old gate and conclusions remain unchanged.
hypothesis: A rest triggered by observed ammunition expenditure can avoid low-value repeated fire commands; aiming width is a simpler competing explanation.

selection.rank: Among eligible candidates, highest Center mean net utility; ties broken by arm name. No Line development evaluation. Select once.

confirmation_arms: Selected candidate, original rules, candidate with rest disabled, command_rest1, and all five preserved history_MAP fits. Same seeds, steering, horizon and action cost; randomized single-worker order.
primary: Selected minus rules and selected minus the mean of the five preserved history_MAP fits in each of two scenarios.

confirmation_gate.interval: 99.375% two-sided paired percentile bootstrap, Bonferroni for four utility and four kill comparisons. Resample seeds and history training fits. Exploratory finite-sample evidence, not guaranteed coverage.

secondary: Matched no-rest and command-rest controls identify simpler explanations; kills, ammo used, actual engine reward, truncations, success and firing windows, total decision compute.
claim_boundary: Handwritten cadence/aiming policy search, not Bayesian RL or a novel architecture. Line was studied previously but excluded from this selection round. Existing evaluation seeds become historical exploratory evidence, never reused as untouched confirmation. Command-window utility may reward suppressing commands; require kill noninferiority and report engine metrics. No claim that hits are per-shot accuracy. No second-environment or adaptive-compute efficacy claims from this study.
